doc: stages/expression.rst, the grammar filters.expression is built on: 'There is no automatic conversion of numeric values to logical values. For example, the following is not permitted: ((Intensity > 0) && Classification). Instead, you must write: ((Intensity > 0) && (Classification != 0)).' -- the page names a form the grammar forbids and the form that replaces it, so both are run here. Run 0 is the forbidden one: the stage must refuse it, the run must fail, and no out.las may be written. Run 1 is the page's own replacement and must succeed; in grid.las every point has a non-zero Classification (1 or 2) and Intensity runs 0..999, so it keeps the 999 points with Intensity >= 1, summing to 499500. The wording of the refusal is NOT asserted -- PROFILE.md 5.3 puts the wording of every rejection diagnostic at this step out of scope -- so what is graded is the exit status and the absence of the output file. The contrasting run is what separates 'the stage is absent' (both runs fail, which is what a 2.4.0 tree does) from 'the stage is present and rejects what the grammar forbids' (only run 0 fails).
